blueprint.title: Deploy the Incident Bundle Indexer
blueprint.scenario: A database administrator is recovering from an incident in which the audit export contained thousands of rotated files in several log formats, and the deployed reconciliation report omitted a small number of important events. The container contains an in-house Node.js indexing tool, deployment wrapper, format documentation, manifests, and a large synthetic incident archive with deliberately rare malformed, duplicated, compressed, and out-of-order records.
blueprint.instruction_draft:
ERROR incident-indexer: published report contains 184,217 events; manifest expects 184,391
WARN deploy: /opt/incident-indexer/current was updated without a successful validation run

Deploy and repair the incident-indexer so the installed command can process an incident bundle from any working directory. It must recursively discover all documented input files, translate every supported input modality into the documented canonical NDJSON output, and apply the documented stream reconciliation rules before producing the report. The result must be deterministic regardless of directory enumeration order, must preserve the documented event ordering, must not double-count records repeated in rotated files, and must exclude records that fail the documented integrity or truncation rules. The deployment must be repeatable, offline, and safe to rerun without leaving a partially published installation.

The deployed command must accept an input directory and output path using the existing interface documented in the repository. It must pass the repository's validation command and process the hidden verification bundles with zero canonical-record mismatches. On the verification machine, processing a bundle containing at least 250,000 physical records must sustain at least 12,000 canonical records per second on one CPU, excluding process startup. Do not hard-code the supplied archive, its filenames, its counts, or its ordering.
requirements: Install a runnable incident-indexer under /opt/incident-indexer/current using the repository's documented deployment interface.
The deployed command must work when invoked from an arbitrary current working directory and must accept the documented input-directory and output-path arguments.
Deployment must be offline, repeatable, and atomic from the observer's perspective: a failed deployment must not replace the last successful installation.
Recursively discover every supported input file in an incident bundle rather than relying on a fixed filename list.
Translate all documented input modalities into the documented canonical NDJSON schema.
Apply the documented integrity, truncation, deduplication, and stream-reconciliation rules to the complete bundle.
Produce deterministic output independent of filesystem enumeration order, process hash-map order, or compression member order.
Preserve the documented canonical event ordering and produce no duplicate canonical event identifiers.
Exclude invalid or incomplete records according to the documented rules without causing valid records from other files or streams to be lost.
Pass the repository validation command and produce zero canonical-record mismatches on hidden verification bundles.
Process a hidden bundle with at least 250,000 physical records at a sustained rate of at least 12,000 canonical records per second on one CPU, excluding process startup.
Do not embed assumptions about the supplied archive's names, counts, ordering, or exact contents.
environment: Use a Dockerfile based on FROM python:3.13-slim-bookworm with pinned apt and pip dependencies and no network access required at runtime; Node.js is installed from a pinned local package during image construction.

Provide approximately 1,400 lines of plausible JavaScript, shell, and documentation across an indexer library, a deployment wrapper, a validator, configuration loaders, and unrelated maintenance utilities.

Provide an existing but broken JavaScript implementation and deployment scripts rather than a toy blank project. The failures are data-dependent and include incorrect handling of rotated-file overlap, global ordering across shards, CSV quoting, gzip members, malformed tail records, and stream state carried across bundle partitions.

Provide documentation describing the supported plain NDJSON, RFC4180 CSV, and concatenated-gzip modalities; canonical fields; event identity; stream sequence and predecessor semantics; integrity checks; truncation behavior; and output ordering.

Provide a large archive under /srv/incident-bundle with thousands of files and hundreds of thousands of physical records. Include rare quoted delimiters, escaped newlines, concatenated gzip members, duplicate rotated ranges, interleaved tenants, out-of-order filenames, incomplete final writes, and records whose validity depends on state accumulated across files.

Provide manifests and small examples that are useful but do not expose every rare combination. Include decoy utilities and stale configuration files so locating the actual production path requires investigation.
Provide a repository validation command that exercises the installed deployment and compares its report with a deterministic oracle.

Provide hidden verify-time bundle generators using fresh seeds, different file partitioning, filenames, compression-member boundaries, stream interleavings, and rare-case frequencies while preserving the documented format and reconciliation contract.

Include a deterministic reference solution as a shell script that first inventories the deployment, documentation, executable behavior, and data distributions, then repairs or replaces the production path and validates it on both ordinary and adversarial bundles.
blueprint.internal_hint: The core failure is not apparent from the small examples. Investigation should begin with the deployment entrypoint and the format documentation, then use scripts to inventory extensions, compression members, duplicate identifiers, sequence gaps, and cross-file predecessor links across the entire archive. The shipped implementation resets stream state at file boundaries, uses filename order as event order, parses CSV by splitting on commas, treats only the first gzip member as input, and handles a truncated final line by aborting the surrounding stream; these defects interact because rotated files deliberately split a tenant's chain and repeat boundary records. A robust repair decomposes discovery/decompression, modality parsing, canonicalization, stateful chain reconciliation, deterministic sorting, and atomic publication. It must maintain per-stream state across all files, deduplicate only according to the documented event identity and overlap rules, validate predecessor and integrity relationships, and use a real CSV parser plus streaming gzip handling. Benchmarking on generated bundles is needed to choose a low-allocation implementation and verify the throughput bar.
blueprint.trap: A shallow solution can pass the visible sample by sorting filenames, splitting simple CSV lines, and keeping a per-file seen set. Hidden bundles reorder files, place quoted commas and escaped newlines in rare records, split gzip data into multiple members, and put the only valid continuation of a stream in a different rotated file. Such a solution either silently loses chained records, accepts an invalid fork, emits duplicate overlap records, or fails the speed threshold after buffering the whole archive.
tests: Run deployment twice and verify that the second run is idempotent, the installed executable works from /tmp, and a deliberately failed candidate deployment leaves the previous installation usable.
Run the repository's validation command on the supplied archive and compare canonical NDJSON records, fields, validity decisions, and ordering against the deterministic oracle.
Generate fresh bundles at verify time with randomized directory trees, filenames, file partition boundaries, and enumeration order; verify byte-for-byte deterministic canonical output.
Generate bundles containing plain NDJSON, RFC4180 CSV with quoted commas and embedded newlines, and concatenated gzip members; verify that all valid records are translated exactly once.
Generate rotated overlaps and duplicates at file boundaries and verify that the documented identity and overlap rules yield one canonical event per event identity.

Generate streams interleaved across many files with predecessor references, gaps, forks, and invalid integrity values; verify that state is carried across files and that only records satisfying the documented reconciliation rules are emitted.
Generate incomplete final writes and malformed records in selected files; verify that permitted truncation is isolated as documented and does not discard valid records from unrelated streams.
Run a large hidden bundle with at least 250,000 physical records on one CPU and fail if sustained canonical-output throughput is below 12,000 records per second, excluding startup.
Check that output contains no duplicate canonical event identifiers, has the documented schema and newline encoding, and contains no temporary-file artifacts after successful publication.

verifier_knob.name: minimum_canonical_records_per_second
verifier_knob.effect: Raising the value forces more streaming, lower-allocation parsing and less redundant rescanning; lowering it permits slower but still correct implementations. Hidden correctness cases remain independent of this performance threshold.

expected_failure_modes: The agent reads the source and patches one obvious parser bug without measuring behavior on the full archive.
The agent assumes lexicographic filename order is the stream order and misses cross-file state reconstruction.
The agent uses String.split for CSV and fails only on rare quoted fields or embedded newlines.
The agent relies on a single gzip decompression stream and silently ignores concatenated members.
The agent deduplicates by a globally incorrect key or resets deduplication at each file, producing either duplicate overlaps or lost distinct events.
The agent buffers all files and obtains correct visible output but exceeds memory or the throughput threshold on hidden bundles.
The agent validates only the supplied archive and hard-codes its observed filenames, counts, or ordering.
The agent modifies the working tree but does not repair the actual deployment path, so hidden tests execute the stale installed command.
The agent publishes output directly and leaves partial reports or a broken installation after an injected validation failure.

speedrun: 1. Inspect the repository tree, deployment entrypoint, and installed-path layout.
2. Read the format, reconciliation, integrity, truncation, and ordering documentation.
3. Inspect package scripts, the existing indexer, deployment wrapper, validator, and configuration loaders.
4. Inventory archive extensions, gzip members, manifests, duplicate identifiers, sequence gaps, and cross-file predecessor links.
5. Run the existing deployment and validation command to capture baseline failures and counts.
6. Patch recursive discovery and stable input ordering without relying on filenames for event order.
7. Replace CSV splitting with an RFC4180-capable streaming parser.
8. Add concatenated-gzip member handling and isolated malformed-tail behavior.
9. Implement canonicalization for every documented modality and schema.
10. Rework reconciliation to retain per-stream state across files and bundle partitions.
11. Implement documented predecessor, integrity, fork, gap, truncation, and overlap rules.
12. Implement identity-based deduplication across rotated files without collapsing distinct events.
13. Implement deterministic canonical ordering independent of enumeration, hash-map, and gzip-member order.
14. Repair the deployment wrapper to resolve paths independently of the working directory.
15. Make deployment validation and publication atomic, repeatable, and safe after injected failure.
16. Run the supplied validator and compare output fields, validity decisions, identifiers, and ordering.
17. Exercise arbitrary working directories, repeated deployment, and failed-candidate rollback.
18. Run the supplied or generated adversarial bundles covering CSV, gzip, overlap, interleaving, and truncation cases.
19. Benchmark the large bundle, optimize allocations and buffering if needed, and rerun correctness tests.
20. Perform final deployment and validation checks, including temporary-artifact and duplicate-identifier checks.
invalid_failure_risks: The exact reconciliation and truncation semantics are delegated to repository documentation that is not included in the blueprint, so an incomplete or contradictory document would make failures ambiguous.
The throughput threshold may vary with CPU model, filesystem behavior, Node.js version, output destination, and benchmark warmup; the measurement protocol needs to be fixed precisely.
Failure-injection tests for atomic deployment can be flaky unless the injection point, process synchronization, and observer behavior are specified.
The definition of which files are supported and how unknown extensions or malformed compression members are handled may be underspecified.
The availability and exact version of the pinned local Node.js package and all build-time dependencies must be guaranteed for the described offline image build.
Hidden generators must preserve the documented contract; otherwise failures could reflect unsupported cases rather than incorrect implementations.
review.reasons: The task is realistic and largely verifiable, but its core defects are discoverable directly from the source and documentation, making a successful path plausible in about 20 commands; under the stated rubric, genuine_difficulty therefore scores at most 2. Since every score must be at least 3, the blueprint cannot be accepted.
fixes: Move the central reconciliation invariant into a less obvious runtime interaction or require behavior that cannot be inferred from a straightforward source reading, while retaining precise documentation of the contract.
Add multiple independently interacting hidden invariants, such as crash recovery during publication combined with resumable processing or bounded-memory requirements verified separately.
Specify the benchmark protocol completely: CPU allocation, filesystem, warmup, output sink, timing interval, process flags, and whether compression and validation are included.
Provide an explicit versioned format specification covering unknown files, malformed gzip members, truncation scope, forks, gaps, and ordering ties.
Define deterministic deployment-failure injection points and the observer’s polling protocol.
Ensure the offline build artifact contains and verifies all pinned local packages before task execution.

verdicts.reason: The candidate centers on recursive multimodal archive indexing, stream reconciliation, rotation-aware deduplication, deterministic ordering, and atomic deployment rather than validating and ingesting a single NDJSON file.
The reference is a stateful TCP HMAC service with binary serialization and refund resolution, whereas the candidate is an offline filesystem archive indexer and deployment workflow.

Although both involve record validation and deduplication, the reference is a chunked CSV ETL pipeline while the candidate requires multimodal log canonicalization, stream reconciliation, and atomic installation.
The reference concerns compiling and deploying WAF rules and classifying HTTP requests, not reconstructing canonical events from heterogeneous incident archives.
The reference is about correcting cryptographic session-key derivation across encrypted log windows, whereas the candidate concerns archive discovery, parsing, reconciliation, and deployment.
